meta.subject: Information and Communication Technology
meta.chapterTitle: Types and components of computer systems
meta.title: Smartphones, tablets and phablets

topics.tablet-disadvantages: Disadvantages of tablets compared with laptops
topics.mobile-uses: Uses of smartphones, tablets and phablets

objectives: Describe smartphones, tablets and phablets and identify their main features
Describe how a proximity sensor and an accelerometer help a smartphone
Give advantages and disadvantages of smartphones and tablets compared with laptops
Compare smartphones, phablets and tablets using the textbook's size guide

learn.title: A smartphone is a computer too
learn.body: A **smartphone** can make telephone calls, but it also has an **operating system** that runs **apps**. It can send emails, take photos, record video and play music. It connects to the internet through **Wi-Fi** or a **3G, 4G or 5G mobile network**. This means you can use many online services while travelling.

learn.alt: Three plain unbranded touch-screen devices, showing a small smartphone, a medium phablet and a larger tablet in order of screen size
learn.caption: Textbook size guide: smartphone, phablet and tablet, from smaller to larger screens.
learn.imagePrompt: Clean educational flat illustration on a pale background. Show three unbranded touch-screen mobile devices side by side: a small smartphone, a medium-sized phablet and a larger tablet. Keep their relative sizes clear and realistic. Use simple blank coloured screens, soft teal and amber colours, gentle shadows. No text, no numbers, no logos, no brand names, no symbols or labels.

learn.title: Smartphone parts and features
items: **Display:** a clear, high-resolution screen, often designed to reduce glare
**Cameras:** front and rear cameras for photographs, videos and video calls
**Bluetooth:** a short-range wireless link to devices such as printers
**Storage:** flash memory in the phone and cloud storage to back up or sync files
**Proximity sensor:** senses when the phone is close to an ear, helping prevent accidental screen touches
**Accelerometer:** senses movement and position so the screen can turn between portrait and landscape
**Speech recognition:** lets a person speak a request instead of typing it
**OLED screen:** a touch-screen technology the textbook links with thinner and lighter phones

learn.title: Using a smartphone: benefits and limits

rows.label: Carrying it
rows.a: Small and light, so it is easy to carry
rows.b: Its small size makes it easier to lose or steal

rows.label: Internet
rows.a: Can use Wi-Fi and mobile networks while moving
rows.b: Mobile data may transfer more slowly than Wi-Fi

rows.label: Screen and input
rows.a: Touch screen and apps are ready to use
rows.b: Small screen and keyboard make reading and typing harder

rows.label: Power
rows.a: Battery life is useful compared with a laptop
rows.b: Photography and web use can drain the battery quickly

rows.label: Files and websites
rows.a: Cloud storage can back up and sync files
rows.b: Less storage than many laptops; some website features may not work

learn.title: What is a tablet?
learn.body: A **tablet** is a portable computer with a **touch screen**. It normally uses a **virtual keyboard**: the keys appear on the screen and you tap them with a finger or stylus. A separate keyboard can also be added. Tablets connect using Wi-Fi or, on suitable models, mobile networks. Like smartphones, they can have cameras, microphones and movement sensors.

learn.title: Advantages of tablets over laptops
items: **Fast start:** a tablet can be ready to use very quickly
**Portable:** a tablet is light and easy to take with you
**Touch input:** you can select items without a separate mouse or keyboard
**Built-in apps:** a tablet can already take photos and play media
**Less heat:** solid-state parts produce little heat
**Battery:** tablets can have longer battery life than laptops
**Standby:** some tablets stay connected and receive alerts while on standby

learn.title: Disadvantages of tablets compared with laptops
items: **Typing:** the on-screen keyboard can be slower and cause more mistakes
**Storage:** tablets often have less space for files
**Software:** laptops usually run more kinds of programs and open more file formats
**File transfer:** moving files can be less direct than dragging and dropping on a laptop
**Mobile data cost:** frequent internet use over a mobile network can be expensive
**Price:** the textbook notes that tablets can cost more than comparable laptops

learn.title: Where does a phablet fit?
learn.body: A **phablet** is a device between a smartphone and a tablet. It combines a larger screen with smartphone features. In the **textbook's size guide**, a smartphone screen measures **up to 5.1 inches**, a phablet screen measures **between 5.1 and 7 inches**, and a tablet screen measures **over 7 inches**. These measurements refer to screen size.

learn.title: What people use smartphones, tablets and phablets for
items: **Entertainment and gaming:** streaming music, videos and TV; playing games with friends
**Camera:** photos and videos almost as good as a digital camera
**Internet:** online shopping, social networks, scanning QR codes, email and instant messaging
**Maps (GPS):** finding the way to a place
**Calendar and banking apps:** organising your day; sending and receiving money
**VoIP:** phone and video calls over the internet
**Education and business:** learning apps; quick voice and video meetings
**Remote control:** using an app to switch home devices on or off from far away, e.g. an oven

learn.title: Choose a device for a school trip
learn.body: A student wants to take photos and send an email while walking between museums. A smartphone is easy to carry and can use a mobile network away from school Wi-Fi. Another student wants a larger screen for reading notes on the bus. A tablet gives more screen space, but typing a long report on its virtual keyboard may be slower than using a laptop.

learn.title: Link a feature to its benefit
learn.body: In a **describe** or **explain** answer, add how the feature helps. For example: 'The phone has a proximity sensor. It stops accidental taps when the phone is held near the user's ear.' For a comparison, name both devices: 'A tablet uses an on-screen keyboard, whereas a laptop has a physical keyboard.'

learn.title: Do not mix up sensors or screen sizes
learn.body: A **proximity sensor** detects nearby objects. An **accelerometer** detects movement and orientation. They do different jobs. Also, the textbook does not call a phablet the biggest device: it places phablets **between** smartphones and tablets in screen size.

learn.title: Textbook predictions versus today's devices
learn.body: The textbook describes possible future phone screens with solar power and **Li-Fi**, which sends data using visible light rather than radio waves. It presents faster transfer and less radio interference as possible benefits. These are not features you should assume every smartphone has. The textbook's screen-size limits are also a teaching guide; present-day device categories can overlap. For questions based on these pages, use the textbook's stated categories.

check.prompt: Which feature detects that a phone is held close to the user's ear?
check.hint: Think about what should happen to the display while someone is making a call, rather than how the phone moves.
check.explanation: A proximity sensor notices a nearby object, such as an ear. An accelerometer notices movement and orientation.

check.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement about smartphones is true or false.
check.hint: Separate connection methods from movement detection, then compare the usual display sizes of handheld devices.

rows.statement: A smartphone can use Wi-Fi to connect to the internet.
rows.explanation: Wi-Fi is one way a smartphone goes online.

rows.statement: An accelerometer is mainly used to detect when the phone is next to an ear.
rows.explanation: That is the job of a proximity sensor.

rows.statement: Smartphones can use Bluetooth to connect to another device.
rows.explanation: Bluetooth can link a smartphone to a nearby printer or another device.

rows.statement: A smartphone always has a larger screen than a tablet.
rows.explanation: The textbook places tablets above smartphones in screen size.

check.explanation: Two correctly classified rows earn one mark.

check.prompt: Complete each sentence using one word or phrase from the list. Use each answer once.
check.hint: All three answers are key words from this mission. Read each whole sentence, then pick the word that fits its meaning.

items.sentence: A tablet's on-screen keys make up a ___.
An ___ can tell when a device changes from portrait to landscape position.
A device with a screen size between a smartphone and a tablet is a ___.

check.explanation: The extra terms were distractors. A phablet is the middle-sized category in the textbook's guide.

check.prompt: Match each smartphone or tablet feature to its main purpose.
check.hint: Think about what each feature actually does when you use it on a phone or tablet.

right.text: Take part in a video call
Control a device with spoken requests
Detect when a device is tilted

check.explanation: Cloud storage handles files, the front camera can show the user in a call, and speech recognition processes spoken commands.

practice.prompt: Give three features of a smartphone other than making telephone calls.

markPoints.point: Can send and receive email
Has cameras for photos / videos / video calls
Uses Wi-Fi / 3G / 4G / 5G for internet access
Runs applications / apps
Uses Bluetooth to connect to nearby devices
Has flash memory / cloud backup and syncing
Has a proximity sensor / accelerometer / speech recognition

practice.modelAnswer: A smartphone can send and receive email. It has front and rear cameras for photographs or video calls. It can use Bluetooth to communicate with nearby devices.
practice.explanation: Give three separate features. Naming the same camera feature in several ways does not earn extra marks.

practice.prompt: State two advantages of using a smartphone rather than a laptop when travelling.

markPoints.point: Smaller / lighter / easier to carry than a laptop
Can make telephone calls on the move
Can use mobile phone networks to go online away from Wi-Fi
Apps can use sensor information / location to show maps
Has useful battery life compared with laptops

practice.modelAnswer: A smartphone is small and light enough to carry easily. It can use a mobile phone network to access the internet while travelling.
practice.explanation: The question asks for advantages while travelling, so focus on portability and using phone or internet services on the move.

practice.prompt: Describe how two different smartphone sensors help a user. Name each sensor and describe what it does.

markPoints.point: Proximity sensor
Detects the phone near the ear / blocks accidental screen touches
Accelerometer
Detects movement / orientation so the display can change between portrait and landscape

practice.modelAnswer: A proximity sensor detects nearby objects. It helps prevent accidental screen touches when the phone is by the user's ear. An accelerometer detects the phone's movement and orientation. It allows the display to change between portrait and landscape.
practice.explanation: One mark is for naming each correct sensor. A second mark for each is earned by describing the correct function. Do not swap the two functions.

practice.prompt: A field worker visits several remote sites each day. She must take photographs and send reports to her office while travelling. Explain two ways a smartphone would help her do this work.

markPoints.point: Smartphone has a built-in camera
So she can photograph site conditions without carrying a separate camera
Smartphone can connect through a 3G / 4G / 5G mobile network
So she can email / send reports from sites without Wi-Fi
Smartphone is small / light
So she can keep it with her when moving between sites

practice.modelAnswer: A smartphone has a built-in camera. She can take pictures of site conditions without carrying another camera. A smartphone can use a mobile phone network. She can send reports to her office while travelling away from Wi-Fi.
practice.explanation: Explain means give the feature and link it to this worker's job. Two different feature-and-benefit pairs earn four marks.

practice.prompt: Give three disadvantages of using a tablet instead of a laptop for schoolwork.

markPoints.point: Typing on the touch keyboard is slower / more error-prone
Often has less memory / storage than a laptop
Supports fewer file formats / less software than a laptop
File transfer can be harder / drag-and-drop may be unavailable
Mobile network use can be expensive
Tablets may cost more than comparable laptops

practice.modelAnswer: Typing on a tablet's virtual keyboard can be slower and cause mistakes. A tablet often has less storage space than a laptop. A laptop usually supports more kinds of software and file formats.
practice.explanation: Give three different drawbacks. They must be disadvantages compared with using a laptop for school tasks.

practice.prompt: Compare a tablet and a laptop for entering text and working with files. Give four differences, stating both sides of each comparison.

markPoints.point: Tablet usually uses on-screen keyboard whereas laptop has a physical keyboard
reject: laptop virtual keyboard and tablet physical

markPoints.point: Typing on a tablet is slower / less accurate whereas typing on a laptop is quicker / more accurate
Tablet often has less storage whereas laptop often has more
Tablet may support fewer file formats whereas laptop supports more
Tablet file transfer may lack drag-and-drop whereas laptop can drag and drop files
Tablet may need app-based transfer whereas laptop allows more direct file handling

practice.modelAnswer: A tablet normally has a virtual keyboard, whereas a laptop has a physical keyboard. Typing can be slower on a tablet, whereas it is usually faster on a laptop. A tablet often has less file storage, whereas a laptop has more. A tablet may open fewer file formats, whereas a laptop supports a wider range.
practice.explanation: Each difference needs both devices. A statement about only tablets is not a complete comparison.

practice.prompt: A student wants a device that can make phone calls and use apps, but has a larger screen than a smartphone and is smaller than a tablet. Explain why a phablet fits these needs.

markPoints.point: Phablet combines features of a smartphone and tablet / is a hybrid
Has a larger screen than a smartphone
Has a smaller screen than a tablet
Keeps smartphone features such as apps / calls

practice.modelAnswer: A phablet combines phone and tablet features. It has a larger screen than a smartphone. Its screen is smaller than a tablet's screen, so it meets the student's size requirement.
practice.explanation: A phablet sits between the other two devices in the textbook's screen-size guide, while keeping smartphone functions.

practice.prompt: Give two disadvantages of using a smartphone rather than a laptop.

markPoints.point: Small screen / keyboard makes pages difficult to read
Typing is slower / more difficult
Web browsing / photography quickly drains the battery
Smaller memory / storage than a laptop
Not all website features work on smartphones
Easier to lose / be stolen
Mobile network data rate can be slower than Wi-Fi / streaming suffers

practice.modelAnswer: The small screen makes web pages difficult to read. It is easier to lose a smartphone or have it stolen.
practice.explanation: Any two valid points. Each must be a disadvantage of the smartphone, not of the laptop.

practice.prompt: Give three advantages of using a tablet rather than a laptop.

markPoints.point: Very fast to switch on / no wait for the operating system to load
Fully portable / lightweight
Touch screen is simple to use / no other input devices needed
Several apps as standard, e.g. built-in camera, media player
Produces little heat (solid-state technology)
Much longer battery life
Stays connected in standby so alerts are still received

practice.modelAnswer: A tablet is very fast to switch on. It is lightweight, so it is easy to carry anywhere. It has a much longer battery life.
practice.explanation: Any three valid points. The book lists: fast to switch on, portable, simple touch screen, built-in apps, little heat, long battery life, alerts in standby.

practice.prompt: Give three uses of smartphones, tablets or phablets.

markPoints.point: Entertainment / streaming music, video, TV
Gaming
Camera / taking photos or videos
Internet use / online shopping / social networks / QR codes
Sending / receiving emails / instant messaging
GPS / maps to navigate
Calendar functions
Telephone / mobile banking
VoIP / video calling
Education / business management
Remotely controlling devices at home

practice.modelAnswer: Streaming music and videos. Using maps to find the way. Remotely switching on devices at home using an app.
practice.explanation: Any three different uses from the textbook list.

summary: Smartphones make calls and run apps; they use Wi-Fi or mobile networks to get online.
Smartphone hardware includes cameras, Bluetooth, flash memory, cloud syncing and sensors.
Proximity sensor: nearby object. Accelerometer: movement and orientation.
Smartphones are light and easy to use on the move, but small screens and keyboards make some tasks harder.
Tablets use touch screens and virtual keyboards; they start quickly but can be awkward for typing and file work.
Textbook screen-size guide: smartphone up to 5.1 inches; phablet 5.1–7 inches; tablet over 7 inches.

flashcards.front: How can a smartphone connect to the internet?
flashcards.back: Through Wi-Fi or a mobile phone network such as 3G, 4G or 5G.

flashcards.front: What does a proximity sensor do?
flashcards.back: It detects nearby objects, helping prevent accidental touches when the phone is near an ear.
It detects movement and orientation, allowing the screen to rotate.
A keyboard shown on a touch screen and operated by tapping the keys.

flashcards.front: Give two tablet disadvantages compared with laptops.
flashcards.back: Typing may be slower and less accurate; tablets often support fewer file formats.

flashcards.front: What is a phablet in the textbook's size guide?
flashcards.back: A phone-tablet hybrid with a screen between 5.1 and 7 inches.
